institution_involved: WNBA and Women's National Basketball Players Association (WNBPA)
source_title: WNBA And WNBPA Reach Tentative Agreement On Groundbreaking Eight-Year Collective Bargaining Agreement
source_description: On January 14, 2020, the WNBA and WNBPA announced a tentative collective bargaining agreement that included increased player compensation, improved travel standards, maternity benefits, childcare support, and other workplace benefits. The announcement describes negotiated changes to player employment conditions.
documented_response: The WNBA and WNBPA announced the tentative agreement jointly. The announcement described the negotiated changes and the organizations' stated goals for improving compensation and the player experience.
uncertainty_context: This is an official announcement from the negotiating organizations, so it reflects their account of the agreement. It does not independently establish discrimination or explain every reason for the prior working conditions. The agreement was tentative when announced.

event_title: Change in WNBA maternity-leave pay under the 2020 CBA
institution_involved: WNBA and Women's National Basketball Players Association (WNBPA)
source_description: The conference-call transcript states that the previous maternity-leave guideline provided half of a player's salary. Under the 2020 agreement, the league committed to full salary during maternity leave. The transcript also discusses expanded family-planning and childcare benefits.
documented_response: The WNBA and WNBPA negotiated a new collective bargaining agreement that expanded maternity and family benefits for players.
uncertainty_context: This is an official transcript of the negotiating organizations' statements, not an independent investigation. It documents a change in employment benefits but does not by itself establish discriminatory intent or explain every player's experience under the previous policy.

event_title: Dearica Hamby Files EEOC Pregnancy Discrimination Complaint
source_title: WNBA player files discrimination claim over treatment during pregnancy
source_description: The Washington Post reported that Dearica Hamby filed a gender discrimination complaint with the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission in 2023. Hamby alleged that after she disclosed her pregnancy, the Las Vegas Aces' coach questioned her pregnancy and commitment to the team, and that she was subsequently traded to the Los Angeles Sparks.
documented_response: Hamby filed a complaint alleging discrimination. The Aces and WNBA were involved in the dispute, and the league conducted an investigation.
uncertainty_context: These details describe reported allegations and responses, not a finding that every allegation was proven. The source reflects reporting about the complaint and does not establish every party's intent.

event_title: WNBA Announces Full-Time Charter Flights for All Teams
source_title: WNBA Set to Institute Full Charter Program During 2024 Season
source_description: The WNBA announced expanded charter-flight arrangements for teams, addressing travel conditions for players.
documented_response: The league announced charter flights for all teams.
uncertainty_context: This record documents a league policy announcement. It does not, by itself, establish the full impact on player safety, competitive fairness, or gender inequality.

event_title: WNBA Sponsorship Campaign Sparks Discussion of Unequal Brand Opportunities
date: November 16, 2024 (article publication date; campaign date unconfirmed)
institution_involved: SKIMS, WNBA players, and corporate sponsors
source_title: WNBA corporate sponsorship deals are growing. But not every athlete is getting their due
source_description: An Associated Press report published November 17, 2024, discusses unequal endorsement opportunities during the WNBA's growing sponsorship market. Natasha Cloud and Natasha Howard criticized a SKIMS campaign for excluding masculine-presenting athletes. The report includes player statements and expert commentary suggesting that race, sexual orientation, and gender presentation can affect athletes' media visibility and access to brand deals.
documented_response: Natasha Cloud publicly criticized the campaign, and Natasha Howard discussed the difficulty Black LGBTQ+ athletes face in obtaining major brand deals. Cloud and Howard subsequently partnered with Woxer, whose founder described the partnership as a good fit. The AP reported that SKIMS did not respond to its request for comment.
uncertainty_context: This record documents reported concerns and examples, not proof that every sponsorship decision was discriminatory. The article includes player accounts and expert analysis, but does not establish the motivations behind every brand's decisions. The exact date of the campaign is not specified in the report summary, so the event date should be checked against the full article before finalizing.

source_title: WNBA: Regular season attendance up 48 percent
source_description: Reuters reported that average regular-season attendance rose from 6,615 fans per game in 2023 to 9,807 in 2024, a 48% increase. The WNBA reported 2,353,735 total attendees, 154 sellouts compared with 45 in 2023, and 22 regular-season telecasts averaging at least one million viewers.
documented_response: The WNBA announced the attendance figures. Reuters attributed much of the increased interest to Caitlin Clark's impact and also reported attendance and performance milestones involving other players.
uncertainty_context: This article documents reported growth in attendance and television audiences; it does not establish that all players benefited equally or explain the causes of gender inequality. The figures are attributed to the league, and the article does not independently establish how increased visibility affected individual players' compensation or sponsorship opportunities.

event_title: WNBA Announces Long-Term Media Rights Agreements
institution_involved: WNBA, The Walt Disney Company, Amazon Prime Video, and NBCUniversal
source_title: WNBA secures landmark media rights deals with The Walt Disney Company, Amazon Prime Video and NBCUniversal
source_description: The official announcement described renewed partnerships with Disney and Amazon Prime Video and a new agreement with NBCUniversal. Beginning with the 2026 season and running through the 2036 season, the partners were scheduled to distribute more than 125 regular-season and playoff games nationally each season. The announcement also described plans for international distribution and rotating WNBA Finals coverage.
documented_response: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert described the agreements as evidence of growing interest and as a way to support the league's long-term growth. Representatives of the media partners also expressed support for expanding distribution.
uncertainty_context: This is an official announcement describing agreements and planned distribution beginning in 2026. It does not independently demonstrate the resulting audience size, how revenue would be allocated to players, or whether all players and teams would benefit equally. Those outcomes require separate evidence.

event_title: Opinion Article Calls for WNBA Player Salaries to Reflect League Growth
institution_involved: WNBA, Women's National Basketball Players Association (WNBPA), and media-rights partners
source_title: It's time for player salaries to catch up with WNBA's growth
source_description: In this opinion article, Caroline Fitzgerald argues that WNBA player compensation has not kept pace with the league's growth. The article compares reported salary caps and player compensation in the WNBA and NBA, discusses revenue sharing, and cites growth in attendance, merchandise sales, viewership, social-media engagement, and media-rights agreements.
documented_response: The article reports that the WNBPA opted out of the existing collective bargaining agreement in October 2024 and was working to negotiate a new agreement prioritizing player compensation and a different revenue-sharing arrangement.
uncertainty_context: This is an opinion article, and its argument that player compensation should rise is the author's position. The article's numerical comparisons and revenue-sharing figures are reported claims that should be checked against their underlying sources before being treated as established facts. The article does not itself establish the final outcome of collective bargaining or how revenue is distributed to each player.

event_title: WNBA Reports Record Viewership, Digital Engagement, and Merchandise Sales in 2024
institution_involved: Women's National Basketball Association (WNBA) and its broadcast and commercial partners
source_description: The WNBA reported more than 54 million unique viewers across national networks, 136.29 million hours of national-network viewing, a 601% year-over-year increase in merchandise sales through WNBAStore.com and its New York flagship location, nearly 2 billion social-media video views, and 366% growth in League Pass subscriptions. The release also reported that games aired or streamed in 207 countries and territories.
documented_response: The WNBA presented these figures as evidence of growth during the 2024 season and highlighted increased audience engagement, merchandise sales, and international distribution.
uncertainty_context: This is an official league press release, so the figures are reported by the WNBA rather than independently audited within the release. The attendance statistics overlap with the existing Reuters record and should not be counted as a separate attendance event. Growth in viewership and sales does not establish that players benefited equally or that gender inequality decreased.

event_title: WNBPA Opts Out of the 2020 Collective Bargaining Agreement
institution_involved: Women's National Basketball Players Association (WNBPA) and Women's National Basketball Association (WNBA)
source_title: WNBA players union decides to opt out of current collective bargaining agreement
source_description: The WNBPA opted out of the 2020 collective bargaining agreement, opening negotiations over a new agreement. The union identified priorities including a more equitable economic model, higher salaries, retirement benefits, child-care and family-planning support, and improved professional working conditions. The WNBA commissioner said the league looked forward to working with the union on a new agreement.
documented_response: The WNBPA initiated the opt-out on behalf of the players. The WNBA publicly welcomed negotiations. The existing agreement remained in effect through the 2025 season.
uncertainty_context: The opt-out created an opportunity to negotiate; it did not itself increase salaries or guarantee the union's requested changes. The priorities described are the union's position and should not be treated as evidence that all demands were accepted. The event is cross-checkable against the WNBA's official FAQ and the league's October 21, 2024 statement.

event_title: WNBA Players and League Remain Far Apart in July 2025 CBA Talks
institution_involved: Women's National Basketball Players Association (WNBPA) and Women's National Basketball Association (WNBA)
source_title: WNBA has failed to meet players' priorities in CBA talks, union says
source_description: Reuters reported that more than 40 players met with league representatives in Indianapolis during collective bargaining discussions ahead of the 2025 All-Star Game. The WNBPA said the league's response did not address key priorities, including a larger share of league business revenue, improved working conditions, and benefits for future players. The league described the discussions more positively and said it was willing to continue negotiations.
documented_response: The WNBPA publicly reiterated its priorities and willingness to continue negotiating. The league indicated that discussions would continue. The 2020 CBA remained in effect during the 2025 season.
uncertainty_context: This record documents the state of negotiations on July 17, 2025, not the final outcome of the bargaining process. The union and league characterized the meeting differently. Their statements represent competing institutional perspectives, and the report does not establish that either side's proposed economic terms were fair or ultimately accepted.
